questions.question: Briefly explain the main differences between a subquery and a Common Table Expression (CTE). Give a short SQL example that shows the same logic written once as a subquery and once as a CTE, and state one situation where a CTE is preferable.
questions.expected_answer:
A subquery is a SELECT nested inside another query (in the WHERE, FROM, or SELECT). A CTE is defined with WITH name AS ( ... ) before the main query. Differences: CTEs improve readability by naming intermediate results, can be referenced multiple times in the main query, and make complex queries easier to understand. Example: Subquery:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name
FROM customers c
JOIN (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders_count FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) o
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.orders_count > 5;
As a CTE:
WITH orders_count AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders_count FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name
FROM customers c
JOIN orders_count o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.orders_count > 5;
When preferable: use a CTE when the intermediate result is used more than once or to make a long query easier to read and maintain.
questions.user_answer:
Differences:

A subquery is nested inside a query and exists only in that context.

A CTE (WITH clause) defines a named temporary result set that can be referenced multiple times in the main query or for readability.
questions.followup_question: Please provide a short SQL example that shows the same logic once as a subquery and once as a CTE (e.g., joining customers to an aggregated orders subquery/CTE).
questions.followup_answer:
Subquery version: SELECT c.id, c.name, o.total_spent
FROM customers c
JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_spent
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND order_date < '2024-01-01'
    GROUP BY customer_id
) o ON c.id = o.customer_id;


CTE version: WITH customer_totals AS (
    SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_spent
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND order_date < '2024-01-01'
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT c.id, c.name, ct.total_spent
FROM customers c
JOIN customer_totals ct ON c.id = ct.customer_id;
questions.feedback: Excellent — clear, accurate definitions; both subquery and CTE examples are correct and equivalent; and the stated reason (readability and reuse of intermediate results) is concrete and appropriate.
